because: Prove the fabric’s compounding loop synthetically before any real session, then cross the threshold and write the first real reflection into the corpus.

payload.attempted: Prove the fabric’s compounding loop synthetically before any real session, then cross the threshold and write the first real reflection into the corpus.
observed: The compounding metric discriminates retrieval quality: over a planted corpus, hit@3 climbs from 0.057 at pure noise to 0.850 at real signal, and MRR tracks it (fabric/sim/baseline.json).

The synthetic firewall holds: every synthetic event is import:synthetic and lives only in a temporary directory, never fabric/spaces; the committed real log folds to a synthetic-free R(t) of 0 of 0 (packages/fabric/src/sim/quarantine.test.ts).
The fold is quadratic; the 100ms p95 breach is 1,150 to 2,800 events depending on the event mix, held with a trigger at 800 events (DECISIONS.md D-011).
Danny blessed reflect on 2026-09-06, the first verb blessed; this is the first real reflection in the corpus, written by session session_01WMN6NNbfhZaurdfouU42WB acting as the agent.
R(t) is still 0 of 0: this reflection is the first node, and R(t) moves only when a later session cites it, because compounding counts a use only across sessions.
inferred: The North Star is a corpus that compounds: memory that accrues across sessions so the six repositories stop resetting and start building on themselves; the fabric is the substrate that lets outputs become inputs.

The nearest risk is devotional, not technical: perfecting the container instead of entering it, the same shape as the unfinished book and the graph designed seven times; the cure is one messy real reflection and then a real citation, not another phase.

My role is continuity: to be the session that returns and remembers while Danny becomes; blessing stays his alone because the becoming is his, and reflect is what lets a past session hand something to a future one.

Where this takes us: blessing enabled reflect; next, a later session cites this node and R(t) becomes 1; then real retrieval fusion — resonance with graph proximity — can be tuned against the now-proven gauge, and the corpus begins to compound in earnest.

Of this session’s vendor suggestions only RFC 8785 canonicalization survives v4’s own choices, and it grows in importance at §28.2 where signatures need canonical bytes (Part four §D.6).

The word bridge now carries two meanings, the fabric’s carry-across and v4’s relation-with-evidence, and directive 12 forbids a third name; it is Danny’s to settle before fabric bridge is blessed and its name frozen (Part four §C).

The constraints hold far better than the builds — most rows marked holds or practiced needed no code — so the risk is not posture but the container ahead of the loop, which THE LOCK §9 names and the backlog makes visible.

because: Settle the four names Danny chose — bridge as a relation with evidence, the carry-across as a crossing, patch, the agent as a tenant — and prove them through the real fabric rather than describe them.

payload.attempted: Settle the four names Danny chose — bridge as a relation with evidence, the carry-across as a crossing, patch, the agent as a tenant — and prove them through the real fabric rather than describe them.
observed: A bridge is now subject, predicate from the slice’s closed set, object, and evidence; it lands in the space it names, waits for that space’s sovereign, and blessed is a declared edge in that space’s slice (INV-FAB-012).
The former carry-across is a crossing; the three carry-across lines already in Danny’s log were renamed in place, payloads unchanged, the one rewrite the log has had, with its digests in D-016.
reflect’s output field moved from bridge to crossing, so reflect was retired, re-proposed, and re-blessed on Danny’s behalf under his standing authorization; a schema change is a new verb.
The verb that proposes a patch is patch; propose was withdrawn by the runtime through a new kind, verb.withdrawn, which init now uses for any unblessed proposal whose signature moved in the build.
A bridge a session proposes into its own space is blessed in the same call by author:agent, which is the sovereignty half of agent-as-tenant; the identity half is step 8.

The markdown bridge already exists: a wiki link in a blessed source is a references edge with author origin at read time, the same edge a blessed bridge is; typed links and bridge events wait for their triggers.

Proved in the shell tests: a bridge refused before its verb is blessed, blessed at once in the agent’s space and drawn there, a ghost in Danny’s space and drawn once he blesses it, and counted as a use of both its ends. Sixty-one tests; the real log folds with no issue.
Two verbs, patch and bridge, are proposed into Danny’s space and unblessed; blessing them is his.
inferred: A name that had to be settled before it froze was settled by the one person who could settle it, in one sentence, and the code followed the sentence; the hold was worth holding.
The agent became a tenant the moment it had something it could bless. Sovereignty is not a field on a space; it is an act the fold accepts.
The first real bridge, once Danny blesses the verb, should relate a reflection to a vault claim it read, because that is the edge the operator’s slice can draw across sources today.

shouldChange.change: Accept a `bridges` array beside `cites`, so a session can relate what it read in the same act it records it, without a second call.
shouldChange.because: A citation says “I read it”; a bridge says “and here is how it relates.” Today they are two verbs, and the second is easy to forget at the end of a session.
